_comment: Controlled vocabulary for Trader Foundation transcript cleanup. Run find-and-replace against every raw transcript before tagging or indexing. Add every new error found. Case-insensitive matching on 'wrong', preserve sentence casing on replace.
_note_on_written_sources: Worksheets are typed, not transcribed, so they carry no mis-hearing errors and are authoritative for numbers and settings. Where a worksheet and a transcript disagree on a value, the worksheet wins. Where they disagree on teaching, that is a ruling for Vlad, not a correction.

confirmed_corrections.note: Full-bodied candle. Japanese term. Students searching the transcript spelling find nothing.
Ticker AM. Ontario Midstream Partners does not exist. High risk: a bot would cite a fictional company confidently.
CONTEXT DEPENDENT. Verify each hit manually before replacing. Two occurrences in Module 5, both in the instigating-event passage.

CONTEXT DEPENDENT. 'demand' heard as 'the man'. Confirmed by the next sentence, which reads 'That means that demand is higher.' Scoped to this full phrase deliberately: a bare 'the man' to 'the demand' rule would corrupt legitimate uses elsewhere.

numeric_corrections._comment: HIGHEST RISK CLASS. The transcription tool mis-hears the numeric values being taught. More dangerous than proper-noun errors: a student who reads 'Mirabozor' can tell something is wrong and search for the right word, but a student who reads a wrong Fibonacci level cannot tell, and the bot would state it confidently as house teaching. Every taught number must be checked against the values established earlier in the same transcript.

instances.note: Fibonacci retracement level. The module establishes 38.2, 50, and 61.8 earlier and uses them correctly four times before this. 32.8 is not a Fibonacci level.
Same lesson, second numeric error, in the passage explaining why the instructor would not take the trade. 60.8 is not a Fibonacci level.

instances.wrong: look at the 250 day moving average. They are way below
instances.right: look at the 50 and 200 day moving averages. They are way below
instances.note: 250 is not a canonical period. Resolved because 'They are' is plural, and 50 plus 200 is the only plural reading in the canonical set. The passage is the background-check step of the method chain, where 50 and 200 are exactly the pair used.

instances.wrong: So here we have the MACD. You could see the MACD represents 80 and 20 right here.
instances.right: So here we have the stochastics. You could see the stochastics represents 80 and 20 right here.
instances.note: Indicator mislabel rather than a bare number error. 80 and 20 with a 50 midline are stochastic bands; the MACD is a centered oscillator around zero. Confirmed by the next sentence, 'On the MACD, you got the two lines as well', where 'as well' marks the switch to a different panel. Left uncorrected, the bot would teach the wrong indicator's bands.

instances.wrong: One could be, let's just say, a 12 day moving average. One could be a 25 day moving average
instances.right: a 12 day moving average... a 26 day moving average
instances.note: RESOLVED BY WRITTEN SOURCE. The Bounce Profit Plan worksheet specifies MACD parameters as 12.26.9, which is also the standard default. The transcript's '25' is a mis-hearing of 26. The same lesson elsewhere says '13 and 28 day moving averages' while reading a blurry on-screen label, which the worksheet also overrides.

instances.wrong: bouncing off both the 20 day moving average and the 30 day moving average
instances.right: bouncing off both the 20 day moving average and the 13 day moving average
instances.note: The module teaches exactly four averages: 13, 20, 50, 200. There is no 30 day. Resolved with confidence because 'both' pairs it with the 20, and 13 is the other short-term average. A second '30 day' occurrence in the Zoom walkthrough has no such pairing and is left unresolved.

formatting_artifacts._comment: The tool splits decimals across a space or a line break, rendering 38.2 as '38. 2'. Cosmetic, but it breaks any numeric check run against the raw text and must be normalised before the values can be audited.

indicator_parameters._source: The Bounce Profit Plan worksheet, which is written and therefore not subject to transcription error. Prefer these over any value read off a transcript.

indicator_parameters.note: RULED: Full Stochastics at 14.3.3, see rulings/stochastics.md. The Momentum video's preference for fast stochastics is superseded. RSI and all other indicators are supplementary to volume, candlesticks and context, see rulings/indicator-hierarchy.md.

screening_filters.52_week_high_low: new high for bullish breakout, new low for bearish breakdown

canonical_values.note: The levels and periods the curriculum teaches. Any other value appearing in a retracement or moving-average passage is a transcription error, not a variant teaching. Two short-term averages (13, 20) and two long-term (50, 200).

generic_transcription_noise._comment: Not proper nouns. Systematic mis-hearings and stray words the tool inserts. Fix per hit, do not run as blind find-and-replace. Found in the Volume module, expect the same class across the library.
